clue.text: Halt a jam that's disrupted tourist site

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traffic jam brought to a halt near a famous monument has spoiled a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges HALT A JAM into the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The white marble mausoleum at Agra in India draws millions of visitors and is a classic example of a tourist attraction.

clue.text: Time to choose accomplished site for leading consumers

parts.note: to opt is to choose
able means skilled, accomplished

explanation.surface: It is time to pick a skilled venue for the most important customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The consumers are diners: the most important guests at a wedding or banquet are seated here.
explanation.definitionFit: The table at a formal dinner where the chief guests sit and eat is the place for the principal diners.

clue.text: Writer getting delight with church

parts.note: joy is delight
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An author is delighted to go to church.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce was the Irish novelist who wrote Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: James, the Irish novelist of Ulysses, is an example of an author.

clue.text: Africans involved in clash anticipated

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped up within the letters of the two words, so involved in signals a hidden word

explanation.surface: Africans were caught up in an expected confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' points to the letters inside clASH ANTIcipated.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of Ghana in West Africa, so a specific group of Africans.

clue.text: Assistant having a plan snubbed

indicators.note: snubbed in its sense of cut short, like a snub nose, so the last letter of the plan word is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A helper's scheme was rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' cuts the final A from IDEA, leaving IDE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide-de-camp is someone who assists a senior figure, a synonym.

clue.text: Small restaurant includes new meal

indicators.note: the small restaurant takes the abbreviation for new inside itself, so includes signals a container

parts.note: a diner is a small, simple restaurant

explanation.surface: A little eatery offers a newly added main course.
explanation.definitionFit: The main evening meal of the day is the usual sense; a synonym for a substantial repast.

clue.text: Restaurant linked to a state

parts.note: an Indian is a curry restaurant, as in going out for an Indian

explanation.surface: A restaurant has ties to a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'an Indian' is a restaurant serving Indian food.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in the Midwest, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Recent grade — and given in French course

parts.note: new means recent
a mark is a grade given for work
the word and, given in French, is et

explanation.surface: A fresh score of ten out of ten has been awarded in a French lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a racecourse: Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous racecourse in Suffolk, England, so an example of a racing track.

clue.text: Enjoy appetizer?

definitions.meaning: to take great pleasure in something, to savour it
a tangy sauce or pickle that whets the appetite; the question mark flags the stretch

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to savour or take pleasure in, and as a noun a chutney or pickle served to sharpen the appetite.

clue.text: Extra note, yes, about Chinese journalist prepared?

parts.note: PS (postscript) is a note added at the end of a letter
Y is a short form of yes, as in Y/N on forms
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
up and about: someone who is about is up, out of bed

explanation.surface: A reporter adds a postscript agreeing to write about a Chinese story, asking if that will do.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order: 'about' comes before Chinese in the clue but its letters come last.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mentally geared up and keyed for an ordeal is to be ready for it; the question mark flags the loose, informal sense.

clue.text: Appropriate limits to tiny piece of land

parts.note: proper means appropriate, fitting

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from tiny

explanation.surface: A fitting cap is placed on a very small plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits to' takes the first and last letters of tiny, T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or real estate one owns is called this, so it names a plot or estate.

clue.text: Pin stuck in window elaborately

indicators.note: the answer is lodged within the run of letters across the two words, so stuck in signals a hidden word

explanation.surface: A pin has been fixed into a window frame in a fussy, ornate way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' shows the answer sitting inside windOW ELaborately.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden peg used in joinery to hold two pieces together is a kind of fastening peg.

clue.text: An egg I boiled getting more advanced?

indicators.note: boiling churns things about, so the letters of the three words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boils an egg for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiled' rearranges AN EGG I. The question mark admits that growing older is a cheeky reading of becoming more advanced (in years).
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older means becoming more advanced in years, which is the whimsical sense the question mark points to.

clue.text: Number methods probed by lawyer currently

parts.note: Number gives NO

indicators.note: the methods are entered by the lawyer, who sits inside them, so probed by signals a container

parts.note: ways are methods of doing things
DA, district attorney, is the American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer currently investigates a number of methods.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the US term for a district attorney, a public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at the present time, these days; a straight adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Tactics from English guy disheartened after nervy start

indicators.note: the English guy comes after the jumbled start, so after orders the charade
nervy means jittery and agitated, so the letters of start are jumbled
losing its heart means the middle letter of guy is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: An Englishman loses heart after a jittery beginning and has to think again about his plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervy' rearranges START into STRAT; 'disheartened' removes the U from GUY, leaving GY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan of action designed to achieve a goal, a near synonym for a set of tactics.

clue.text: Drink taken by male in principal vessel? It has unforeseen effects

indicators.note: the drink and the male go inside the word for principal, so in marks the container

parts.note: lead as an adjective means principal or chief, as in the lead role

indicators.note: the drink is taken along by the male, which joins the two side by side

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, a drink
he is the male pronoun
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's boat

explanation.surface: A man downing a beer aboard the flagship sets off consequences nobody could predict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' sets the male right after the drink, and 'in' puts that pair inside the principal. The definition is a whole phrase: such a venture is one whose results cannot be foreseen.
explanation.definitionFit: A risky step taken with no idea of the outcome is a venture whose consequences cannot be predicted, an idiom for a gamble.

clue.text: Statement made by discordant air's notes

indicators.note: discordant means jarring and out of harmony, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune whose notes clash makes a strong declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discordant' rearranges AIRS NOTES, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm declaration or claim is a kind of statement.

clue.text: Police in corrupt state provide searching examination

indicators.note: the police go inside the rearranged state, so in marks the container
corrupt means spoiled and twisted, so the letters of state are rearranged

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges the letters of state to ATEST, and 'in' places the detectives inside that; the state is no country at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial of worth, from the use of acid to test gold, so a rigorous examination.

clue.text: Firearm came out with its aim suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or unsound, so these letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A gun emerged, its target questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges CAME OUT plus ITS AIM; 'with' only joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that reloads itself after each shot but needs a separate trigger pull is a type of firearm.

clue.text: Wandering direction taken by malicious German article

parts.note: mean means unkind or malicious
der is the German masculine definite article, the

explanation.surface: A spiteful German takes a rambling route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding, aimless course, like a river's loops, is a rambling path.

clue.text: Heavy rain shortly appearing after start of week

indicators.note: the word for shortly turns up after Monday's abbreviation, so these words order the charade

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated Mon, begins the working week
soon means shortly, before long

explanation.surface: A downpour is forecast for early in the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing after' puts the word for shortly behind the start of the week, which is not its first letter but the whole short form of Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South Asia brings torrential downpours, so the word names that wet season's deluge.

clue.text: Inactive plant nearly visible

indicators.note: only nearly all of the plant word shows, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: statice, also called sea lavender, is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A dormant shrub can hardly be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Statice is a flower often dried for arrangements; with its last letter hidden it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Not moving or changing, motionless, is a synonym for inert or still.

clue.text: Indicate menace afterwards about drug hoarded by despicable chap

indicators.note: the word for afterwards goes round the rest, so about signals a container

parts.note: then means afterwards, next

indicators.note: the drug is stashed away inside the despicable chap, so hoarded by marks a container

parts.note: a rat is a despicable person, a traitor
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Later a contemptible man is found stockpiling narcotics, a sign of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarded by' tucks the drug inside the despicable chap, and 'about' wraps the word for afterwards round that.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn of harm or be a sign of coming danger is to menace, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Whole college followed by boy

indicators.note: the college comes first and the boy after it, so followed by orders the charade

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
Ted is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A student goes to college and a lad comes along afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined into one, combined, is the sense of whole, entire, as in a single unified body.

clue.text: Hint about western intonation

indicators.note: the hint goes round the western letter, so about marks a container

parts.note: a tang is a hint or trace of a flavour

explanation.surface: A suggestion about a cowboy's drawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal or regional quality in speech is a kind of accent or tone of voice.

clue.text: Fellow leaving limited cheese

indicators.note: the fellow departs from the word for limited, so leaving signals a deletion

parts.note: brief means short, limited in time

explanation.surface: A man walks off without his small piece of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with a white rind, so an example of cheese.

clue.text: Criminal gang, one in recurrent gossip

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip, as in dishing the dirt

explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' turns DIRT into TRID, and A goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese organised crime syndicate is called this, so it is a specific example of a criminal gang.

clue.text: Narrow glass for a day troubled the French

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of these three words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: le is the French for the

clue.text: Singer making clamour about an African initially

indicators.note: the word for clamour wraps around the rest, so about marks a container

parts.note: a cry is a loud call, a clamour

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word African

explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow finch kept as a cage bird and prized for its song, so a songbird or singer.

clue.text: Celebration for birds before a match?

definitions.text: Celebration for birds before a match?

parts.words: Celebration for birds before a match?
parts.note: birds is British slang for women, and a match is a wedding: a bride and her female friends party before the big day

explanation.surface: A party for feathered friends ahead of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a bird is a woman, and the bride-to-be is the female of the farmyard pair.
